title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the fourth version of 'Analysis situs' (1986), Grothendieck axiomatizes a combinatorial framework for 'figures' and their decompositions.

The framework, as far as the surrounding pages let us reconstruct it:
- A 'magasin' is a set M of decomposed figures with two orders and one map.
  - X <= Y: X is a subfigure (sub-decomposition) of Y.
  - X << Y: X is a refinement of (a part of) Y.
  - |.|: the underlying-figure map, X -> |X|.
- X~ denotes the set of pieces (cells) of the decomposition X.
- Omb(Y') is the 'shadow' of a piece Y'. This reading is inferred, not defined on this page.
- The magasin is subject to axioms Mag 1 - Mag 4.
- On the previous page Grothendieck contrasted two points of view:
  - 'spacieux' (general spaces), with relations << and not-overlapping;
  - 'polyédral' (standard piecewise decompositions), with relations <<_pol and not-overlapping_pol.

First part of this page. Grothendieck observes that inside the magasin the two points of view barely differ:
- the data are the same;
- the polyhedral case only adds one stricter axiom, 'Mag pol'.

Mag pol: if X << Y and Y' is a piece of Y, then the set of pieces of X lying in the shadow of Y' is either empty or has a greatest element. This expresses that every refinement X << Y is automatically a polyhedral refinement X <<_pol Y.

Order-theoretically, take the 'carrier' map X~ -> Y~, which sends each piece of X to the piece of Y it refines (cf. Mag 2' b on the next page). Mag pol says this map has a partial right adjoint: a partial Galois connection between the poset of pieces of X and that of Y.

He adds that one will still need, besides (or instead of) the non-overlap relation, a polyhedral non-overlap relation.

Second part. He returns to the axiomatics Mag 1 - Mag 4 and notes that << is recovered from the immediate-refinement relation <<° together with <= by

(*) X << Y  <=>  there exists Y' with X <<° Y' <= Y.

Every refinement thus factors as an immediate refinement of a subfigure. He then asks when a structure (M, <=, <<°, |.|) comes from a magasin. Two conditions are needed:
- (a) << defined by (*) satisfies the magasin axioms;
- (b) the immediate-refinement relation of that magasin is exactly <<°.

The next page carries this out. The key conditions are:
- a distributive or 'interchange' law: X <= Y <<° Z implies there exists Z' with X <<° Z' <= Z;
- uniqueness of the factorization.

Together these make the composite relation <= o <<° transitive. The result is a reaxiomatization Mag 1' - Mag 4'. In categorical language, it is a strict (unique) factorization system on the preorder generated by the two relations.

Purpose: to set up a flexible combinatorial 'tame topology' of figures and their decompositions. The program is to replace general topology by a theory of figures and their standard decompositions, in the spirit of the Esquisse's 'topologie modérée'.
errors: No outright error. The sentence 'la connaissance de <<°, |.| redonne celle de <<' is slightly off as transcribed. The equivalence (*) only uses <<° and <=, so the relevant data are (<<°, <=). The written symbol may in fact be <= rather than |.|.

As written, Mag pol is clear only once Omb (shadow) and the ordering on pieces are fixed; these are defined on earlier pages. Under a naive reading (pieces of a subdivision inside a closed cell), a 'greatest element' would fail. So the intended order on pieces must be specific, e.g. the face order with a carrier/collapse interpretation.
In (*), transitivity of the composite relation requires the interchange law (2) stated on the next page. Antisymmetry is not addressed on this page.

ideas.what: Extra axiom distinguishing polyhedral from general ('spacieux') refinement inside an abstract poset-with-refinement structure ('magasin'): pieces of X in the shadow of a piece of Y have a maximum
ideas.modern_name: partial right adjoint / Galois connection condition on the carrier map between face posets; cellular refinement vs arbitrary refinement
ideas.usually_credited_to: no direct analogue; related to combinatorial approaches to tame topology and o-minimal / PL cell decompositions
ideas.where_published: Only the general program of 'topologie modérée' is in Esquisse d'un programme (1984); the magasin axiomatics is unpublished as far as known

ideas.what: Recovering the refinement relation from immediate refinements and inclusion via unique factorization X <<° Y' <= Y
ideas.modern_name: unique factorization of morphisms (strict factorization system / distributive law between two relations, Zappa–Szép-type interchange)
ideas.usually_credited_to: factorization systems: Freyd–Kelly (1972); distributive laws: Beck (1969)

ideas.what: Reaxiomatization question: when does (M, <=, <<°, |.|) come from a magasin
ideas.modern_name: presentation of a structure by generating relations and interchange laws

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'magasin' axiomatics for figures and decompositions (Mag 1-4, Mag pol), with the spacieux/polyédral dichotomy expressed as a single order-theoretic axiom, is an unpublished concrete attempt at the 'tame topology' foundations announced in Esquisse. He also flags a polyhedral non-overlap relation still to be developed.
missed.quote: Cela n'empêche qu'il faudra par la suite, en plus de ≭ (ou au lieu de ≭), introduire la relation ≭_pol
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a possible combinatorial axiomatization of tame/PL decompositions. It could be compared with o-minimal cell decompositions and with combinatorial models such as face posets and exit-path categories. The axiom is modest, however, and depends on definitions given on earlier pages.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a page of axiomatics bookkeeping. The order-theoretic content (unique factorization, interchange law, a partial-adjoint condition) is routine. Interest lies only in its being part of the little-known unpublished 'magasin' framework for tame topology.
transcription_corrections: 'Mag rel' should read 'Mag pol' (underlined). Similarly 'X ≪_rel Y' should read 'X ≪_pol Y', consistent with the previous page.

'en plus de ≪̸ (ou au lieu de ≪̸), introduire la relation ≪̸_rel' should read 'en plus des ≭ (ou au lieu de ≭), introduire la relation ≭_pol'. The symbol is the non-overlap relation, not 'not refines'.
'l'axiomatique que je base' is more likely 'que j'ai basée'.
'la connaissance de ≪°, |·|' may read '≪°, ≤', since (*) uses ≤.
'Dans le magasin, la différence des deux points de vue se réduit au minimum: on ne la voit pas dans la notion des données' is confirmed, with 'et des axiomes' struck out.
Bottom: 'quand ... validée(s) (M, ≤, ≪°, |·|), celle-ci provient d'un magasin'. The inserted word appears to be 'validées' or 'relations', and is uncertain.
